newsitem.title: UK: HSBC estimates edge up but provisions loom.
newsitem.headline: HSBC estimates edge up but provisions loom.

text.p: Banking analysts were on Monday looking to marginally raise their 1997 estimates for HSBC Holdings Plc after the banking giant posted a 23 percent rise in 1996 profits to 4.52 billion stg.
But some expect little growth for HSBC's profits over the year with John Aitken of UBS estimating 4.65 billion stg, adding that he might raise this by just 50 million stg.
Aitken sees the spectre of higher provisions against bad debts this year and was surprised by the higher level of provisions at Hongkong Bank and Hang Seng Bank, of which HSBC owns 61 percent.
He also sees higher debt provisions in Britain and the U.S. and also expects most of HSBC's territories to experience downward pressure on margins.
At Morgan Stanley, banking analyst Nick Collier expects 1997 pre-tax profits of around 4.94 billion and was also considering a small upside revision.
Collier said the results were "a good clean set of figures" although he admitted to being slightly surprised by the level of provisions in Hong Kong.

HSBC's bad debt charge overall fell to 384 million stg from 416 million in 1995 but this hid a rise in Hong Kong from 25 million stg to 143 million stg and an overall 11 percent rise in new specific provisions to 740 million stg.
Non-performing loans in Hong Kong rose to 320 million stg from 166 million in 1995.
HSBC chief executive said there had been one or two problem accounts in Hong Kong but that the bank had not discovered a trend or pattern.
"It's just part of the regular risk we run in our business," Bond said, adding that no particular sector had been at fault.
